info.title: Stash Studio API
info.description:
APIs for querying a shop's managed product catalog and loyalty program, for configuring the loyalty program from a partner's own tools, for asking Stash to refresh a shop's localizations, and for listing a shop's daily transaction files and downloading them through signed links. Designed for server-to-server communication between partner backends and Stash services.

## Base URLs

| Environment | Base URL |
|---|---|
| **Test** | `https://test-api.stash.gg` |
| **Production** | `https://api.stash.gg` |

All endpoint paths below are relative to the base URL. For example, to list products in the test environment:

```
GET https://test-api.stash.gg/sdk/studio/{shop_id}/products
```

## Authentication

Every request is signed with your Ingress API key (HMAC-SHA256). Send the signature in the versioned `x-stash-hmac-signature` header.

### Setup

1. Go to **Stash Studio > Project Settings > API Secrets**
2. Click **Generate Secret** to create a new key
3. Keys created through this portal are Ingress keys by default and work with this API (this is the same key used for `/sdk/` API authentication)
4. Copy the key and store it securely; you will need it to sign every request. Studio shows the key Base64-encoded: keep it as shown, and Base64-decode it to raw bytes when you sign

### Signing a Request

1. Take the current time as a Unix timestamp in **milliseconds**, for example `1790000000000`
2. Build the string to sign as `{timestamp}.{body}`. For GET requests `{body}` is empty. For PUT and POST requests it is the **request body exactly as you send it** (the same bytes; do not re-serialize the JSON after signing). Stash verifies the signature against those exact bytes for bodies up to 18 KiB (18,432 bytes); a larger body may be refused with `401` even when it is correctly signed
3. Base64-decode your Ingress API key to raw bytes, compute HMAC-SHA256 of that string keyed with those bytes, and Base64-encode the result. Signing with the encoded key text produces a signature Stash rejects
4. Send the header `x-stash-hmac-signature: v1;{shopId};{timestamp};{base64Signature}`. The timestamp must be within 5 minutes of Stash server time

### Example (bash and python)

Keep the key, exactly as Studio shows it, in a file with owner-only permissions or in a secret store, and read and Base64-decode it inside the signing process. Never pass it as a command-line argument: process listings and shell history can capture it.

```bash
# sign <body>: prints the header value for the exact body you are about to
# send. Every request gets its own timestamp and signature.
sign() {
  local ts sig
  ts=$(($(date +%s) * 1000))
  sig=$(TS="$ts" BODY="$1" python3 - <<'PY'
import base64, hashlib, hmac, os
key = base64.b64decode(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.stash/ingress-key'), 'rb').read().strip())
msg = (os.environ['TS'] + '.' + os.environ['BODY']).encode()
print(base64.b64encode(hmac.new(key, msg, hashlib.sha256).digest()).decode())
PY
)
  printf 'v1;%s;%s;%s' '{shop_id}' "$ts" "$sig"
}

# GET: the signed body is the empty string.
curl -H "x-stash-hmac-signature: $(sign '')" \
  "https://test-api.stash.gg/sdk/studio/{shop_id}/products"

# PUT: sign the exact bytes you send, then send them with --data-binary,
# which keeps them intact. -d @file strips newlines, so the server would
# see different bytes from the ones you signed and reject the signature.
BODY='{"campaign":{"id":"season-1","name":"Season 1","tiers":[]}}'
curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-stash-hmac-signature: $(sign "$BODY")" \
  --data-binary "$BODY" \
  "https://test-api.stash.gg/sdk/studio/{shop_id}/loyalty/config"
```

### Legacy header (deprecated)

`stash-hmac-signature` carries an untimestamped Base64 HMAC-SHA256 of the body alone (empty string for GET). Only four read endpoints still accept it: `GET /sdk/studio/{shop_id}/products`, `GET /sdk/studio/{shop_id}/products/{product_id}`, `GET /sdk/studio/{shop_id}/loyalty` and `GET /sdk/studio/{shop_id}/loyalty/players/{player_id}`. It is replayable, so use the versioned header for new integrations. Every other endpoint accepts only the versioned header and answers `401` to the legacy one.

get.description: Retrieves the shop's loyalty configuration in the shape UpdateLoyaltyConfig accepts: display settings, bonus definitions, reward products with their status, every campaign (season) with its status, and the spend conversion table with the rate derived per currency. Product rewards are returned by SKU. Use it to verify a sync. This method accepts only the versioned x-stash-hmac-signature header, signed over an empty body; the legacy stash-hmac-signature header is rejected with HTTP 401 (UNAUTHENTICATED), because it carries no timestamp and a captured request could be replayed. Errors, by the HTTP status a REST caller receives and its gRPC status: 401 UNAUTHENTICATED when the signature is missing, invalid, outside the time window, sent in the legacy header, or names a different shop; fix the signing, because resending it unchanged does not help. 404 NOT_FOUND for an unknown shop or a shop with no loyalty program; it does not change on a retry. 501 UNIMPLEMENTED when the loyalty configuration API is not available; it does not change on a retry. 500 INTERNAL when Stash hits an internal error, for example reading the shop's loyalty configuration; reading is safe to repeat, so retry with backoff.

Must include USD. Each amount is a positive decimal string whose digits past the currency's minor unit are zero, under the minor-unit standard configured for your shop (see `cents` in GetCatalog): JPY "1500" or "1500.00", not "1500.5". Under the default, Unicode CLDR release 32, IDR, COP, PKR and TZS accept only zeros after the point; a shop configured for CLDR release 47 or ISO 4217 may give them two places, for example IDR "1000.50". At most 200 currencies.

put.description: Creates or updates one loyalty campaign (season) together with the shop-level display settings, bonus definitions and reward products it depends on, optionally sets or removes the program-level spend conversion table, and optionally activates the program. The campaign id is the upsert key: an existing id updates that season, a new id creates one. The request describes the whole season it names, so a tier or milestone omitted from it is removed from that season; bonuses and reward products are created or updated by id or SKU and never removed. Draft and scheduled seasons accept every change. An active season accepts names, descriptions, images, milestone rewards, tier earn rates and a new end date; thresholds, adding or removing tiers or milestones, the start date and reset rules are refused with FAILED_PRECONDITION listing the fields. Ended seasons are read-only. This method accepts only the versioned x-stash-hmac-signature header, signed over the request body exactly as sent; the legacy stash-hmac-signature header is rejected with HTTP 401 (UNAUTHENTICATED), because it carries no timestamp and a captured request could be replayed. Applying is idempotent, so resending the same request is safe. Errors, by the HTTP status a REST caller receives and its gRPC status. Two of them share HTTP 400; a REST caller tells them apart by the code in the error body, 3 for INVALID_ARGUMENT and 9 for FAILED_PRECONDITION. 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT (code 3) with per-field violations when validation fails, including a spend conversion price whose rate against the US dollar is more than 3 times above or below the market rate, which the violation on that price names; fix the request, correcting the price, because resending it unchanged does not help. 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 9) when the request cannot apply to the program as it stands, with the reason in the message: for example a locked field of an active season changes (the message lists the fields), the shop has no loyalty program and activate is not set, or the shop's loyalty program is bound to more than one shop; resend only once that changes, or as is when the message says to re-send the request. 401 UNAUTHENTICATED when the signature is missing, invalid, outside the time window, sent in the legacy header, or names a different shop; fix the signing. 403 PERMISSION_DENIED when the shop is not enabled for configuration writes; it does not change on a retry. 404 NOT_FOUND for an unknown shop; it does not change on a retry. 409 ABORTED when another update for the shop is in progress; resend the same request after a short wait, which is safe because applying is idempotent. 501 UNIMPLEMENTED when the loyalty configuration API is not available; it does not change on a retry. 500 INTERNAL when Stash hits an internal error, for example reading or writing the shop's loyalty configuration; resend the same request with backoff. 503 UNAVAILABLE when the request has a spend conversion price in a currency other than USD and Stash has no market rates loaded, for example shortly after a restart; nothing is written, and resending the same request with backoff is safe because applying is idempotent.

spendConversion.description: The shop's spend conversion table, which lets earning convert a purchase in a non-USD currency to its US dollar equivalent. Optional and program-level: it is not part of the season, applies whatever the season's status, and is not subject to the active-season edit lock. Sending it replaces the stored table; omitting it leaves the stored table unchanged; sending it with an empty tiers list, or as the empty object {}, removes the table. With a table stored, the spend of a purchase in a currency the table does not include earns no points, while loyalty points the offer grants as a bonus are still earned (the purchase is never blocked); without a table, earning is unchanged. A change reaches purchases within 30 seconds. A validation failure returns INVALID_ARGUMENT with per-field violations under spendConversion, for example spendConversion.tiers[0].prices.EUR. For each currency other than USD, Stash compares the rate the row implies (the price in that currency divided by the USD price) with the market rate published by the European Central Bank (ECB). If it is more than 3 times above or below the market rate, or the price is worth no US cents at the market rate, the request is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT and nothing is written. The violation is on spendConversion.tiers[0].prices.<CODE> for that currency's ISO code, and its message gives the rate the row implies and, unless the price is worth no US cents at the market rate, the market rate and the factor; correct the price to fix it. A row with no currency other than USD is never checked. A currency the ECB publishes no rate for is accepted, stored unchecked and used for earning, and the response's warnings names it by ISO code.

post.description: Asks Stash to refresh the shop's localizations from its enabled localization source, for example after the source file changes. The request body is the empty JSON object {}. This method accepts only the versioned x-stash-hmac-signature header, signed over the request body exactly as sent ({}); the legacy stash-hmac-signature header is rejected with HTTP 401 (UNAUTHENTICATED), because it carries no timestamp and a captured request could be replayed. The shop in the signature header must equal the shop_id in the path. A successful response means the refresh is durably queued, not that the import has completed or that the storefront shows the result. Repeated calls are safe, so retry after a 500, a 503 or a timeout with a fresh timestamp and signature. Errors, by the HTTP status a REST caller receives and its gRPC status. Two of them share HTTP 400; a REST caller tells them apart by the code in the error body, 3 for INVALID_ARGUMENT and 9 for FAILED_PRECONDITION. 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT (code 3) when the request is malformed, for example a body that is not valid JSON; fix the request, because resending it unchanged does not help. 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION (code 9) when the shop has no enabled localization source; retrying does not help until the source is set up and enabled. 401 UNAUTHENTICATED when the signature is missing, invalid, outside the time window, sent in the legacy header, or names a different shop or one Stash does not know; fix the signing, because resending it unchanged does not help. 500 INTERNAL when Stash hits an internal error, for example reading the shop's localization settings; retry with backoff. 503 UNAVAILABLE when the refresh could not be queued; retry with backoff.

accepted.description: true once the refresh is durably queued; not import completion or storefront visibility.

post.description: Returns one entry for each UTC day in [start_date, end_date] that has a file, in date order, each with a signed GET link to that day's file. A day with no transactions still has a file, with no rows. A day with no entry is a day the export has not written yet, such as the current UTC day or a day whose export is late; it does not mean the day had no transactions, so call again later for that day. Days before first_date never get a file, because the shop's export of that type and format started on first_date. A shop that has no file of the requested type and format on any day gets FAILED_PRECONDITION instead. Stash turns a shop's export on, and it writes the first file, before the partner is told that the report is available; so this error means the report is not available for the shop yet: do not retry, contact Stash. The files use the same columns as the transaction reports in Stash Studio. Each row is one event: a payment, a refund or a dispute step. A later refund or dispute step is a new row on its own day; it does not change the payment's row. The record_id column is a stable ID of the event: the same event has the same record_id in every file. Use it to remove rows that two pulls share, and keep the row from the later pull. Columns are added only at the end, and a column is renamed or removed only with advance notice, so read the files by column name, not by position. A SETTLED day that is not final can still change; pull it again until is_final is true. SETTLED days become final together with their UTC calendar month, when Stash closes the month, usually 1 to 5 days after it ends. CHARGE days are never final, because their rows change while their charges settle, so do not wait for is_final on a CHARGE day. Stash gives no stop signal for a CHARGE day: follow it for as long as you need its unsettled rows, and use SETTLED for figures that become final. To know when to download a day again, compare its content_hash with the copy you hold: every change to the file's bytes gives a new content_hash, and the same bytes always give the same content_hash. as_of is the time of the data snapshot that each file was written from. Every link is valid until download_url_expires_at, 15 minutes after the response; call again for fresh links. This method accepts only the versioned x-stash-hmac-signature header, signed over the request body exactly as sent; the legacy stash-hmac-signature header is rejected with HTTP 401 (UNAUTHENTICATED), because it carries no timestamp and a captured request could be replayed. The shop in the signature header must equal the shop_id in the path. Repeated calls are safe, so retry after UNAVAILABLE or a timeout with a fresh timestamp and signature. Returns HTTP 401 (UNAUTHENTICATED) when the signature is missing, invalid, outside the time window, sent in the legacy header, or names a different shop or one Stash does not know; HTTP 400 (INVALID_ARGUMENT) when report_type or report_format is unspecified or unknown, a date is missing or is not YYYY-MM-DD, end_date is before start_date, or the range is longer than 31 days; HTTP 400 (FAILED_PRECONDITION) when the shop has no file of the requested type and format on any day; and HTTP 503 (UNAVAILABLE) when the files could not be listed, in which case retry. The two HTTP 400 cases differ only by the code in the response body: 3 for INVALID_ARGUMENT, 9 for FAILED_PRECONDITION. Do not retry UNAUTHENTICATED or INVALID_ARGUMENT unchanged: correct the signature or the request first, then send it again with a fresh timestamp and signature.

Always false for CHARGE, which never becomes final: do not wait for true on a CHARGE day. Always sent, including false.

sizeBytes.description: Size of the file in bytes, never negative. Always sent, including 0 for an empty file. JSON carries it as a decimal string.

downloadUrl.description: Signed GET link to the day's file. Valid until download_url_expires_at.

asOf.description: The report cut: the time of the source data snapshot that the file was written from (RFC 3339, UTC). Every row in the file comes from that snapshot. Absent for a file the export wrote before it recorded its snapshot time.

contentHash.description: An opaque hash of the file's bytes. Every change to the file's bytes gives a new value, and the same bytes always give the same value, so download a day again exactly when its content_hash differs from the copy you hold.

A day before first_date, or a day the export has not written yet, has no entry.

prices.description: The price point's amount per currency, keyed by upper-case ISO 4217 code recognized by Stash, for example {"USD": "9.99", "EUR": "9.49", "GBP": "7.99", "JPY": "1500"}. Must include USD. Each amount is a positive decimal string whose digits past the currency's minor unit are zero, under the minor-unit standard configured for your shop (see `cents` in GetCatalog): JPY "1500" or "1500.00", not "1500.5". Under the default, Unicode CLDR release 32, IDR, COP, PKR and TZS accept only zeros after the point; a shop configured for CLDR release 47 or ISO 4217 may give them two places, for example IDR "1000.50". At most 200 currencies.

ratesPerUsd.description: For each non-USD currency in the row, the units of that currency per one US dollar, as a decimal string with exactly four decimal places, for example "1.0000" or "150.1502". Derived and for display only: Stash converts with the exact amounts of the row, never with a rounded rate. Ignored on input.

spendConversion.description: The shop's spend conversion table, which lets earning convert a purchase in a non-USD currency to its US dollar equivalent. Optional and program-level: it is not part of the season, applies whatever the season's status, and is not subject to the active-season edit lock. Sending it replaces the stored table; omitting it leaves the stored table unchanged; sending it with an empty tiers list, or as the empty object {}, removes the table. With a table stored, the spend of a purchase in a currency the table does not include earns no points, while loyalty points the offer grants as a bonus are still earned (the purchase is never blocked); without a table, earning is unchanged. A change reaches purchases within 30 seconds. A validation failure returns INVALID_ARGUMENT with per-field violations under spendConversion, for example spendConversion.tiers[0].prices.EUR. For each currency other than USD, Stash compares the rate the row implies (the price in that currency divided by the USD price) with the market rate published by the European Central Bank (ECB). If it is more than 3 times above or below the market rate, or the price is worth no US cents at the market rate, the request is refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT and nothing is written. The violation is on spendConversion.tiers[0].prices.<CODE> for that currency's ISO code, and its message gives the rate the row implies and, unless the price is worth no US cents at the market rate, the market rate and the factor; correct the price to fix it. A row with no currency other than USD is never checked. A currency the ECB publishes no rate for is accepted, stored unchecked and used for earning, and the response's warnings names it by ISO code.

v1CampaignStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a loyalty campaign (season), derived from the program
state and the campaign window.

 - CAMPAIGN_STATUS_DRAFT: Not visible to players: the season has no start date, or the program is not live.
 - CAMPAIGN_STATUS_SCHEDULED: The program is live and the season's start date is in the future.
 - CAMPAIGN_STATUS_ACTIVE: The program is live and the season's window contains the current time.
 - CAMPAIGN_STATUS_ENDED: The season's end date has passed. Read-only.

warnings.description: Notes on the update, of two kinds. A part of the request that was accepted but had no effect, for example activate on a program that is already live. A currency in the spend conversion table that was stored without a market-rate check because the ECB publishes no rate for it; the note names the currency by its ISO code, and the currency is still stored and used for earning. Empty when there is nothing to report.

prices.description: The price point's amount per currency, keyed by upper-case ISO 4217 code recognized by Stash, for example {"USD": "9.99", "EUR": "9.49", "GBP": "7.99", "JPY": "1500"}. Must include USD. Each amount is a positive decimal string whose digits past the currency's minor unit are zero, under the minor-unit standard configured for your shop (see `cents` in GetCatalog): JPY "1500" or "1500.00", not "1500.5". Under the default, Unicode CLDR release 32, IDR, COP, PKR and TZS accept only zeros after the point; a shop configured for CLDR release 47 or ISO 4217 may give them two places, for example IDR "1000.50". At most 200 currencies.

ratesPerUsd.description: For each non-USD currency in the row, the units of that currency per one US dollar, as a decimal string with exactly four decimal places, for example "1.0000" or "150.1502". updatedAt.description: When the stored table last changed (RFC 3339). Ignored on input.

reportType.description: Which report to list. SETTLED has one file per UTC settlement day, with rows dated by settlement. CHARGE has one file per UTC day, with each row dated by its own Transaction Date: a payment by its charge time, a refund or dispute step by its own time.

reportFormat.description: File format of each link. CSV, JSONL and PARQUET hold the same rows and columns. JSONL leaves a field with no value out of the row's object.

startDate.description: First UTC day of the range, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD. The range [start_date, end_date] is at most 31 days.

endDate.description: Last UTC day of the range, inclusive, as YYYY-MM-DD. Must not be before start_date.

date.description: The UTC day the file holds, as YYYY-MM-DD.

isFinal.description: true when the day's rows are final and no longer change: a SETTLED day becomes final when Stash closes its UTC calendar month. false for a SETTLED day while its rows can still change; pull the day again later. Always false for CHARGE, which never becomes final: do not wait for true on a CHARGE day. Always sent, including false.

sizeBytes.description: Size of the file in bytes, never negative. Always sent, including 0 for an empty file. JSON carries it as a decimal string.

downloadUrl.description: Signed GET link to the day's file. Valid until download_url_expires_at.

asOf.description: The report cut: the time of the source data snapshot that the file was written from (RFC 3339, UTC). Every row in the file comes from that snapshot. Absent for a file the export wrote before it recorded its snapshot time.

contentHash.description: An opaque hash of the file's bytes. Every change to the file's bytes gives a new value, and the same bytes always give the same value, so download a day again exactly when its content_hash differs from the copy you hold.

downloadUrlExpiresAt.description: When every download_url in this response stops working (RFC 3339, UTC), 15 minutes after the response. Set on every successful response, also when files is empty.

firstDate.description: The first UTC day, as YYYY-MM-DD, that has a file of the requested type and format for the shop, even when it is outside the range. Days before it never get a file; a later day with no entry is not written yet.

v1ReportFormat.description:
The file format of a report file. Every format holds the same rows and columns.

 - REPORT_FORMAT_UNSPECIFIED: Refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT.
 - REPORT_FORMAT_CSV: Comma-separated values with a header row.
 - REPORT_FORMAT_JSONL: JSON Lines: one JSON object per row. A field with no value is left out of
the object, not written as null.
 - REPORT_FORMAT_PARQUET: Apache Parquet.

v1ReportType.description:
- REPORT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: Refused with INVALID_ARGUMENT.
 - REPORT_TYPE_SETTLED: One file per UTC settlement day; rows are dated by settlement and reconcile with the payout.
 - REPORT_TYPE_CHARGE: One file per UTC day. Each row is dated by its own Transaction Date: a payment by its charge time, a refund or
dispute step by its own time. Includes unsettled and failed charges.

hmac.description: Versioned HMAC-SHA256 signature for server-to-server requests to this API (your backend calling Stash), as opposed to client-side operations. Recommended over the deprecated legacyHmac scheme for the best security. Header format: v1;{shopId};{unixMillisTimestamp};{base64Signature} (semicolon-delimited). {base64Signature} is the base64-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of the string {unixMillisTimestamp}.{requestBody} signed with your Ingress API key, where {requestBody} is the request JSON exactly as sent for POST and PUT requests and empty for GET requests. The Ingress API key Stash Studio shows is base64-encoded: base64-decode it and use the resulting raw bytes as the HMAC key; signing with the encoded text produces a signature Stash rejects. The timestamp must be within 5 minutes of Stash server time. Your shopId is your immutable shop identifier; it and your Ingress API key are available in Stash Studio under Project Settings > API Secrets.
hmac.name: x-stash-hmac-signature

legacyHmac.description: DEPRECATED: use the versioned hmac scheme (x-stash-hmac-signature) instead for the best security. HMAC-SHA256 signature generated by signing the request body (empty string for GET requests) with the Ingress API key from Stash Studio. Base64-encoded. Accepted only by ListProducts, GetProduct, GetLoyalty and GetPlayerLoyalty; every other ingress endpoint rejects it with UNAUTHENTICATED because it carries no timestamp.
legacyHmac.name: stash-hmac-signature
